title: Send Half of the People to Each City at the Smallest Cost

concept.title: Sort the people by how much cheaper city A is than city B
body: A company must send **exactly half** of `m` people to the city A and the other half to the city B. Person `i` costs `a[i]` to send to A and `b[i]` to send to B. What is the smallest total cost? For the costs `(10,20) (30,200) (400,50) (30,20)` the answer is 110: send the first two to A (10 + 30) and the others to B (50 + 20).

Start by sending **everybody to B**: the cost is the sum of all `b[i]`. Now we must move exactly `m / 2` people to A. Moving the person `i` changes the total by `a[i] - b[i]` (negative when A is cheaper for this person). To get the smallest total, **move the people with the smallest values of `a[i] - b[i]`**. So sort the people by `a - b` and send the first half to A and the second half to B.

body.code:
people.sort(key=lambda p: p[0] - p[1])         # who gains the most by going to A comes first
half = m // 2
total = sum(a for a, b in people[:half]) + sum(b for a, b in people[half:])
print(total)

body: Why does sorting by the difference work? Suppose in an optimal plan person `x` goes to A and person `y` goes to B but `a[x] - b[x] > a[y] - b[y]`. Swapping them (`x` to B, `y` to A) changes the cost by `(b[x] - a[x]) + (a[y] - b[y])`, which is negative, so the plan was not optimal. This **exchange argument** proves that the first half of the sorted list goes to A. The sort costs O(m log m).

statement: `m` people (`m` even) are given with the costs `a` and `b` of sending each of them to the city A and to the city B. Exactly `m / 2` people must go to each city. Print the smallest possible total cost.
inputFormat: The first line has `m`: the number of people (an even number).
Each of the next `m` lines has two numbers `a` and `b`: the cost of sending this person to the city A and to the city B.

examples.note: People 1 and 2 go to A (10 + 30), people 3 and 4 go to B (50 + 20): 110.

hints: Imagine everybody goes to B first; moving a person to A changes the cost by a - b.
Move the m / 2 people with the smallest a - b.
Sort by a - b and cut the list in half.

explanation: Sending everybody to the city B costs the sum of all b; moving a person to A changes the cost by a - b, so the m / 2 smallest differences are added to that sum (equivalently: sort by a - b, the first half goes to A).
solution.complexity: Time O(m log m), space O(m).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

m = int(input())
costs = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

costs.sort(key=lambda p: p[0] - p[1])
half = m // 2
total = 0
for i in range(m):
    total += costs[i][0] if i < half else costs[i][1]
print(total)
